text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Dedicated pool 'lucid-health-dedicated-1' node gpu-node-17 reporting sustained ECC and correctable memory errors. Affected pool: lucidhealth-dedicated (customer: LucidHealth, VPC). Severity: P2. Page sent to on-call SRE.

alex chen: acked. jumping in. starting triage.

alex chen: quick check: `nvidia-smi -q` shows multiple CORRECTABLE ECC errors on GPU 2 and rising GPU memory CRCs. host shows kernel ring buffer grep for "NVRM: Xid" with repeated entries.

raj singh: thanks alex. pulling task placements. looks like 3 LucidHealth model-serving pods on that node (serving-lg-onnx-01, reranker-02, task-embed-03). One is currently at ~85% GPU mem.

sophie li: passing note — this pool is reserved for LucidHealth (contracted capacity). we need to avoid any data crossing tenants; don't migrate pods to non-dedicated pools. plan should prefer other GPUs in the same dedicated pool.

alex chen: agree. immediate plan: cordon node and drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` after ensuring replicas on other GPUs in same pool. I'm going to check if there are valid placement targets.

infra-bot: Autoscaler snapshot: dedicated pool lucidhealth-dedicated has 8 total GPUs across 4 nodes, 2 spare GPUs currently available (pending autoscaler thresholds). No active scaling operations.

mira patel: quick customer impact check: are there request errors now or just degraded perf?

alex chen: current metrics — 5xxs are spiking from reranker-02 (those pods on gpu-node-17) 1.2% -> 4.8% last 10min. Latency P95 for that model went 350ms -> 980ms. So ongoing customer impact for a subset of requests.

se-lucidhealth: (LucidHealth SE): we see increased errors in our dashboards too. We have live inference traffic for health-check endpoints, some retries are happening. Please advise on impact windows.

alex chen: brief to SE: we're going to cordon and try to drain and relocate pods to other GPUs in your dedicated pool. That may cause short connection drops (<30s) during restart. We'll coordinate more if we need to evict with force.

raj singh: validating replica counts and affinity: two of the three pods have nodeAffinity tied to dedicated pool labels only, so they can land on other nodes in the pool. Good. One pod is hostNetworked (can't be moved) — it's an edge case, might need manual failover within the app.

alex chen: starting safe drain runbook: 1) cordon node 2) set graceful termination to 60s for impacted deployments 3) `kubectl drain` 4) monitor healthcheck/SLOs 5) if pods stuck, rollback to snapshot and trigger manual failover. Executing step 1 now.

alex chen: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` -> node cordoned.

deploy-bot: Rolling drain job scheduled: drift-id 4f7c. Expected pod restarts: 5.

sophie li: notifying account manager to prepare a customer message if we see >5 minutes sustained errors. @se-lucidhealth FYI.

alex chen: doing the drain...

alex chen: drain progress: 2/3 pods terminated and successfully rescheduled on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-14. hostNetwork pod (serving-lg-onnx-01) is still on gpu-node-17 and did not reschedule due to hostNetwork requirement. It's the one causing the 5xxs.

mira patel: can we restart that service in-place on another node? If it's hostNetwork maybe it needs manual config change.

raj singh: the hostNetwork pod was pinned by the app team because of 3rd-party licensing tied to host MAC. we need coordination with app-owner to rotate it; can't force-migrate automatically.

alex chen: OK. next options: a) force-restart the node (risky) b) live migrate by creating an alternative non-hostNetwork replica (requires app rollout) c) evacuate traffic by updating routing to fallback model variant. I'll try to drain remainder and then escalate.

infra-bot: Node-level memory errors persist. Kernel Xid errors continuing. Hardware vendor recommended creating a hardware ticket and evacuating node.

alex chen: I'm going to mark the node in 'maintenance' and open a hardware replacement ticket with vendor. Meanwhile we'll update routing to fallback to reduce customer error rate.

alex chen: patching routing for LucidHealth: set route for reranker service to fallback model (cfg: reranker-v2-q4) with lower memory profile. Apply now.

deploy-bot: Route update applied for reranker -> reranker-v2-q4.

sophie li: SE and AM looped. drafting short customer message: "We detected hardware instability in your dedicated pool; we are evacuating the affected node and routing a subset of traffic to a low-memory fallback. Some requests may see brief increased latency while we complete failover." Send after we have acceptance?

se-lucidhealth: understood. please proceed. we'll prepare internal comms. ETA to respond to customers: 10m.

alex chen: after routing change, 5xx rate down from 4.8% -> 0.9% in 3 minutes. latency P95 improved to ~420ms. looks stable but node errs continue.

raj singh: I'm creating a ticket to hardware vendor: Ticket LU-1905-17 - GPU ECC spike on gpu-node-17. Attaching `dmesg` and nvidia logs. Recommend immediate replacement.

alex chen: marking node as unschedulable for long-term: `kubectl label node gpu-node-17 maintenance=true` and `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-17 dedicated=lucidhealth:NoSchedule` so autoscaler won't put new pods there.

alex chen: node labeled and tainted.

mira patel: I'm taking on-call handoff in 12 minutes. will monitor until vendor confirms hardware swap. handing over state: cordon+drain attempted, hostNetwork pod blocked (owner needs to create non-hostNetwork replica), reranker traffic routed to fallback, 5xxs significantly reduced.

alex chen: thanks - created a short runbook in thread for you: 
- watch SLOs for LucidHealth (reranker + serving-lg)
- confirm vendor ticket updates: LU-1905-17
- coordinate with SE for hostNetwork pod plan and iterate with app team tomorrow
- if node errors escalate to uncorrectable (Xid 13+), escalate to infra director and consider forced power cycle

mira patal: (typo) mira patel: got it. I'll take over. ping me if anything flips.

infra-bot: Vendor ticket created: LU-1905-17 (priority: high). Vendor ETA for engineer on-site: 6 hours.

se-lucidhealth: thanks for the quick mitigation. keep us posted if hostNetwork pod needs config changes; we'll prioritize.

alex chen: adding final notes to incident doc and marking this thread for a post-incident follow-up: - action item: app-team to remove hostNetwork requirement or add HA non-hostNetwork replica - action: vendor RMA for GPU board - action: infra to add proactive ECC alert rule for dedicated pools (lower threshold)

mira patel: thanks. handing off fully to me. I'll update status if vendor ETA changes or SLOs degrade.

incident-bot: Incident TODOs: document created incident/1905003333, owner: mira patel, severity: P2, linked ticket: LU-1905-17.

alex chen: thanks all.

mira patel: closing temporary paging for on-call rotation. monitoring continues.

se-lucidhealth: appreciate the quick response :thumbsup:

alex chen: noted for postmortem: consider automatic fallback for hostNetwork-limited pods via shadow replica.

sophie li: filing a follow-up with AM and legal for SLA impact assessment; will attach logs and mitigation timeline.

(END OF THREAD)
